name: UK Funky
summary: Nominally four-on-the-floor house at ~130, defined by the kick breaking into tresillo syncopations for a bar and snapping back, under an Afro-Caribbean percussion engine of congas, cowbells, shakers and rims phrased in 3+3+2. Snares and claps borrow soca's engine-room chatter; hits are stabbing and punchy with a live velocity contour.

sounds.kick: Tight, punchy house kick (909-style) with a short tail; extra syncopated kicks at slightly lower velocity for momentum.
sounds.snare: Crisp clap or clap+snare on 2 and 4, plus a soca-style tight snare for double-16th pickup rolls and offbeat chatter.
sounds.hats: Syncopated offbeat closed hats and a choked open hat into the bar line; never a flat 16th carpet — the percussion does that job.
sounds.percussion: Congas and bongos in call-and-response, cowbell on the tresillo, shakers, woodblock/clave, log-drum style low toms in the afro-swing lane.
sounds.cymbals: Crash on phrase starts; ride uncommon.

machines: Roland TR-727 — congas, bongos, agogo, whistle: the Latin percussion kit (owned)
Roland TR-808 — cowbell, conga and clave (owned)
LinnDrum / Oberheim DMX — sampled congas, tambourine and cabasa (owned)
Korg M1 drums and Roland MC-303 — cheap late-2000s preset kits close to the FL-era sound (owned)
Kontakt 'Laventille Rhythm Section' and Roska's UK Funky sample packs — soca steel-band percussion (get elsewhere)
